new_statements.quote: El proto-idioma seguramente tuvo, aparte del tono, un acento sobre la raíz, que distinguía a ésta de los afijos. En algunas partes de la comunidad dialectal primitiva, el acento caía en la última sílaba de la raíz y sus reflejos se notan en el amuzgo y en el trique; en otras, representadas por el cuicateco y el mixteco, el acento lo llevaba la penúltima sílaba. Actualmente, el mixteco tiene el acento en la posición referida, según observaciones hechas personalmente por la autora, en los diversos dialectos de la costa de Oaxaca. [...] En las cuatro divisiones, el acento pudo omitirse, porque los términos aquí presentados son elementos morfémicos y la posición del acento se desprende de las condiciones generales ya mencionadas.
new_statements.translation: The proto-language surely had, besides tone, an accent on the root, which distinguished it from the affixes. In some parts of the early dialect community the accent fell on the last syllable of the root, and its reflexes are seen in Amuzgo and Trique; in others, represented by Cuicatec and Mixtec, the penultimate syllable [of the root] carried the accent. At present Mixtec has the accent in that position, according to observations made personally by the author in the various dialects of the Oaxaca coast. [...] In the four divisions the accent could be omitted [from the transcriptions], because the items presented are morphemic elements and the position of the accent follows from the general conditions already mentioned.

new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. The quoted accent claim is for 'el mixteco' as a whole, explicitly grounded in the author's observations of Oaxaca-coast dialects, and tone is only 'probablemente' present in all dialects and not recorded; nothing is asserted of Cuyamecalco specifically beyond its inclusion in the word lists. | checker: Arana Osnaya 1959: the whole-issue PDF we hold is live at repositorio.inah.gob.mx (HTTP 200, 43,755,664 B; landing o-9048 HTTP 200). I rendered PDF p. 240 (= printed p. 232) and compared A's quote with the page image line by line: 'El proto-idioma seguramente tuvo, aparte del tono, un acento sobre la raiz.. en otras, representadas por el cuicateco y el…
new_statements.relation_note: Tone exists in probably all Mixtec dialects but marked only for phonemically analysed dialects (not Cuyamecalco); accent root-penultimate in Mixtec generally.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Pan-Mixtec claim (1959): word accent is bound to the root and falls on the penultimate syllable of the (disyllabic) root, i.e. root-/couplet-initial ('acento inicial' in Mixtec and Cuicatec vs root-final in Trique/Amuzgo); accent morphologically conditioned (affixes and non-final compound members unaccented); all Mixtec dialects 'probably' have tone but tone was not recorded for Cuyamecalco.
new_statements.exceptions: Compounds: 'El elemento final lleva acento y el anterior o anteriores carecen de el' (p. 233). No Cuyamecalco-specific exceptions; author lacked adequate prosodic data for most dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for cuya1240 ('Mixteco-Cuyamee' = the 'Cuyamee' column of the diagnostic list). Sources list p. 231: '(cu) Cuyamecalco, Dto. de Cuicatlan, Oaxaca y (sj) San Juanico Cuautzospan, Dto. de Teotitlan, Oax. Roberto Escalante (ENAH)'; her 'grupo 2' = Cuyamecalco + San Juanico (p. 261). Cuyamecalco material is a 100-item glottochronological list (xtu). CAVEAT: the stress sentence is a statement about 'el mixteco' as a whole, evidenced by the author's observations in Coast dialects and applied to all Mixtec forms cited (including Cuyamecalco) - not an observation on Cuyamecalco speech.
